note: Parses the decrypted ticket data into a new SSL_SESSION object. If parsing succeeds, sess points to a valid session.
Computes remaining bytes after the parsed session. If the decrypted ticket contains trailing garbage bytes, slen will be non-zero.

code: if (slen != 0) { SSL_SESSION_free(sess); ret = SSL_TICKET_NO_DECRYPT; goto end; }
note: When extra trailing bytes exist after the parsed session, sess is freed via SSL_SESSION_free() but is NOT set to NULL. This leaves sess as a dangling pointer.
The dangling pointer to freed memory is assigned to the caller's output parameter *psess, propagating the use-after-free condition to tls_parse_ctos_psk.
tls_decrypt_ticket returned SSL_TICKET_NO_DECRYPT, so the loop continues. However, sess still holds the dangling pointer from the freed session.
In the next loop iteration, sess is non-NULL (dangling pointer), so ssl_session_dup() is called on freed memory, triggering a use-after-free.
